evidence.text: On the Q3 call (2026-06-25) the CFO guided Q4 core EBITDA up about $40-50m sequentially from $353.6m (to roughly $394-404m). evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: CMC fell 3.83% to $64.53 on 2026-09-18, the session after both guides (MarketBeat quote page), so the sector's 'below consensus' reset has already been taken. No prior CMC reaction to peer guidance is in the baseline.

evidence.text: The Q1 FY27 call (2026-07-09) said active PaperPie Brand Partners rose from 4,300 (end Feb) to about 5,200 after a March recruiting special and had been 'maintained ... to this day'. A Q2 FY27 average near 5,200 against 5,800 a year ago is about a -10% partner decline, against -31% in Q1 (5,300 vs 7,700) and -58% in Q2 FY26 (5,800 vs 13,900). Applying FY26's Q2/Q1 revenue-per-partner ratio (0.86) to Q1 FY27's ~$898 implies Q2 revenue of roughly $4.0-4.3m against $4.6m: still down, but the smallest year-on-year decline in two years.

evidence.text: The Q1 FY27 10-Q shows the company now records no tax benefit on losses (valuation allowance: $16.5k tax expense vs a $(374)k benefit a year ago), and fixed lease cost after the Hilti leaseback rose to $388k from $171k per quarter. Even if pre-tax loss improves from $(1.8)m to around $(1.4)m, the headline net loss is likely about $(1.4)m, EPS about $(0.16) vs $(0.15): worse year on year at the line the wire prints. Q1 showed exactly this pattern (pre-tax loss flat, net loss $(1.40)m vs $(1.08)m).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 FY27 the same tax swing made net loss and EPS worse year on year while pre-tax was flat, and the stock fell -3.18%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Headline-driven retail and algo readers of a no-coverage microcap see 'net loss widens' without the tax context. Had it been priced as non-cash, the July print would not have sold off on a flat pre-tax loss.
evidence.independence: The Q1 release states the tax effect (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/304633/Educational-Development-Corporation-Announces-Fiscal-2027-First-Quarter-Results). It shares the company as source with the 10-Q, so it is not independent.

evidence.text: Liquidity improved and is not distressed. Q1 FY27 cash rose to $1.66m (+$0.5m) as inventory fell $1.5m to $36.2m. The company is debt-free after the $32.2m HQ sale. CFO: 'turning inventory into cash should translate into positive cash flow.'
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cash up and debt free at Q1 still met -3.18%. The Oct 2025 HQ sale did not lift the stock durably (now -20.6% from its 52-week high).
evidence.why_not_priced: The market cap is about $11m against $36m of inventory, so the market is discounting inventory heavily. A second quarter of inventory-to-cash conversion would be evidence against that discount. Had it been priced, the stock would not sit near its 52-week low. Rule 4: what the money buys is new titles, and Q1 showed new-title releases; the revolver is a positive or zero, not distress.
evidence.independence: The revolver is in the 8-K of 2026-03-11: https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/288147/Educational-Development-Corporation-Announces-New-Loan-Agreement-and-Banking-Relationship
